method: Read all source requests without sampling or prompt/output length scaling.
Render using the local Qwen3.6 HF chat template, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True, preserve_thinking=True.
Sort by original source.startMs; only source requests with source.endMs <= current startMs are available for prefix comparison.
Compare the current prompt token IDs with the latest completed prompt in the same session.
For the all-history upper bound, find the longest token prefix among all completed prompts in a shared tenant. No byte-budget eviction or generated outputs are simulated.
Count distinct complete input token sequences as input-endpoint candidates; these are not required concurrent resident snapshots.

last_token_spotcheck.scope: Illustrates tokenization boundary effects; does not classify every one-token difference.

limitations: Five historical coding-optimizer sessions, not a measurement of all lab users or five simultaneous GPU requests.
Only input prefixes are compared. Output-end reuse, snapshot placement, eviction, GPU admission, transfer latency, and expert-bandwidth competition are unmeasured.
The two-endpoints-per-path count assumes genuinely unbranched extension and excludes explicit anchors, active references, in-flight copies and other cache types.
A token-trie split is not evidence of persistent multi-branch demand; tokenization-tail differences can create splits.
The raw full-length trace need not fit the GPU KV configuration used by scaled serving benchmarks.
